entry.title: QGIS DevTools plugin for easier plugin development
entry.summary: Just came across this new debugging plugin for QGIS called DevTools that was released by NextGIS. The plugin basically lets you connect VS Code to QGIS for debugging. Instead of adding logging statements everywhere or dealing with buggy setups, you can now set breakpoints, inspect variables, and step through your code directly from your IDE. Launches a debugpy server from QGIS Can be configured to start automatically when QGIS launches Allows choosing a custom port for the debug server Lets you connect from VS Code to debug your own plugins Simple setup process Before this, debugging QGIS plugins could be painful. Many developers relied on adding logging messages everywhere or used older plugins like debug_vs_plugin, which was often buggy and had issues on Windows and macOS. This new plugin provides a much more streamlined approach to remote debugging. The plugin is available on the official QGIS plugin repository and the source code is on GitHub. The documentation walks you through the setup process step by step. This seems like a valuable tool for anyone developing QGIS plugins, and its foundation on the modern debugpy library is a promising sign. One current limitation, however, is that debugging code in other threads (e.g., QgsTask) still requires some extra work. Hopefully, future versions will streamline this process. While it did crash QGIS on me once during testing, the core functionality is reliable, making it a clear upgrade from the alternatives. Thanks to the folks at NextGIS for making this - looks like a really helpful tool.
